the AOT algorithm is globally well-posed, globally regular and globally converges to a weak solution of the 3D Navier-Stokes equation, provided that the observations satisfy the aforementioned conditions.
\emph{the AOT algorithm is a viable data assimilation method for the 3DNSE, and is robust to noise in the observations, even for weak solutions of the NSE}.

\emph{The AOT algorithm is well defined and converges, in an appropriate sense, to a global Leray-Hopfsolution of the 3D Navier-Stokes equation, provided only that the observed data satisfies a certain condition.}
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a rigorous mathematical analysis of a data assimilation algorithm, the AOT algorithm, for the three dimensional Naviers-Stokes equations (incompressible fluid dynamics) in order to determine the conditions, \empt{based solely on observations}, that guarantee the well-posedness of the algorithm and the convergence of the data assimilation algorithm to the true solution of the 3D Navier-Stokes equation.
the question, \emph{"Can we use the data assimilation algorithm to recover the global solution of the 3D Navier-Stokes equation, even if it is not unique?"}.
the development of an efficient, robust and computationally tractable numerical scheme that can be used to accurately approximate the solution of the 3D Navier-Stokes system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AOT data-assimilation algorithm is \emph{robust} in that it can be applied to a wide range of solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes system, including those that are globally regular as well as those that are not.

the AOT data- assimilation algorithm, which is a continuous version of the classical Kalman-Bucy filter, can be used to reconstruct the 3D Navier-Stokes dynamics from the available observations, provided that the solution of the 3D- NSE is a weak solution of the Leray-Hopftype.

the AOT algorithm is a viable data assimilation algorithm that can be used to obtain a \emph{global} and \emph{unique} weak solution to the 3D Navier-Stokes equation from noisy and incomplete observations of a \emph{lackluster} weak solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AOT algorithm can be applied to a wide class of weak solutions of the 3D-Navier-Stokes equations and the algorithm will provide a global, unique and regular approximation to the weak solutions.
we have established a rigorous mathematical foundation for the AOT algorithm for 3D Nse.

we show the global existence of a unique solution of the AOT equations, for any Leray-Hopfsolution, and that the solution of the ATO equations converges, in $L_2$, to the true solution, in the absence of any regularity assumptions on the true solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, under the aforementioned conditions on the observation data, the AOT data-assimilation algorithm is capable of producing a global regular solution to the Navier-Stokes equation, even when the original solution is merely a weak solution.
the AOT algorithm is \emph{robust} to the presence of \emph{singularities} in the data.
the AOT algorithm can be used as a \emph{regularizing filter} for the 3DNSE.
